PART I

Item 1. Business

ExampleCo Inc. designs, manufactures and markets consumer electronics, software and related services worldwide. The Company sells its products through its retail stores, online stores and direct sales force, as well as through third-party cellular network carriers, wholesalers, retailers and resellers. The Company's fiscal year is the 52- or 53-week period that ends on the last Saturday of September.

Item 1A. Risk Factors

We depend on a limited number of suppliers for key components.

Substantially all of the Company's hardware products are manufactured by outsourcing partners that are located primarily in Asia. A significant concentration of this manufacturing is performed by a small number of outsourcing partners, often in single locations. If supply of a key single-sourced component were to be delayed or constrained, the Company's business and operating results could be materially adversely affected.

Cybersecurity incidents could disrupt our operations and harm our reputation.

The Company experiences malicious attacks and other attempts to gain unauthorized access to its systems on a regular basis. These attacks seek to compromise the confidentiality, integrity and availability of confidential information and could disrupt the availability of services. Losses or unauthorized access to or releases of confidential information could subject the Company to significant litigation, fines and reputational harm.

The COVID-19 pandemic could continue to disrupt our supply chain and demand for our products.

The COVID-19 pandemic has had, and could continue to have, a significant impact on the Company's operations, including temporary retail store closures, reduced customer traffic and constrained component supply resulting from government-mandated factory shutdowns in regions where the Company's suppliers operate. The duration and severity of future outbreaks remain uncertain and difficult to predict.

PART II

Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

Net sales for fiscal 2022 were $394.3 billion, an increase of 8% compared to fiscal 2021, driven by growth across all product categories. Gross margin percentage was 43.3%. The Company generated operating cash flow of $122.2 billion during fiscal 2022.

Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data

The consolidated financial statements of the Company, together with the report of the independent registered public accounting firm, are included herein. Net sales were $394,328 million and net income was $99,803 million for the fiscal year ended September 24, 2022.
